item.title: Ranji Trophy: Bengal look for hat-trick of wins as Kerala host table-toppers on seamer-friendly track
item.description: If momentum is important in sports, then both Kerala and Bengal will carry it in abundance when they face each other in an Elite Group C Ranji Trophy match at the KCA ground, Mangalapuram, in Thiruvananthapuram on Monday. Fresh from their innings victory against Odisha in their last match, Kerala will have a job in hand to stop an upbeat Bengal who will be looking for a hat-trick of wins after beating Delhi and Services to lie at the top of the table with 12 points in their group. However, Bengal will look for an improved show from their batters after they failed to put up enough runs on board against Services. It was their spinners who did the job for them then, but the KCA ground is unlikely to assist the spinners much. In that case Bengal might go in with three pacers, with Mohammed Shami once again taking up the new ball after the former India pacer sat out in the last game. He will expect good support from his brother Mohammed Kaif and Suraj Singh Jaiswal. Toss is likely to play an important role on a surface which offers early assistance to the pacers. Bengal coach Laxmi Ratan Shukla will look for more runs from the blades of Sudip Chatterjee and opener Ankur Pal as Bengal need to put up a competitive total against a good batting unit that features Sachin Baby, Vishnu Vinod and Mohammed Azharuddin. Much will depend on how the ever-dependent Jalaj Saxena contributes both with the ball and bat. Shahbaz Ahmed will once again play a key role for Bengal, after the all-rounder made an immediate impact on returning from an injury to play his first match in months against Services. However, the weather might play spoiler, with forecasts of occasional rain, which ruined the teams’ practice sessions, over the next few days. But the possibility of a complete washout is remote, and both sides are preparing for a stop-start game.

The Lions were explosive to begin the game and scored a touchdown on their opening drive for the first time all season. item.title: Lazio’s Next Technical Sponsor: Two Companies Vying as Umbro Pull Out
item.description: Lazio’s Next Technical Sponsor: Two Companies Vying as Umbro Pull Out With their collaboration with Mizuno drawing to an end, Lazio are searching for a new technical sponsor and a kit supplier. Lazio to Break Away From Mizuno In 2022, the Biancocelesti struck a five-year contract with the Japanese company worth circa €5 million per season. But it now appears that the two parties are heading in separate directions. Their contract will expire at the end of the 2026/27 campaign, with no signs of a renewal on the horizon. Umbro Pull Out of the Race? Several candidates to replace Mizuno have emerged over the past few days, including Umbro, a choice that evoked nostalgia among Lazio fans, as the famous British manufacturer was Lazio’s kit supplier between 1989 and 1998. But according to La Lazio Siamo Noi , Umbro is losing ground to two other companies. Castore The Favourites to Sign With Lazio? The source identifies Castore as the current favourite to seal the deal. The English company was founded in 2015, but has already built a solid reputation, especially in the British Isles, striking partnerships with Everton and Burnley, among others. Lazio would represent a golden opportunity for the company to enter the Italian market. Hummel Join the Race While Castore are looking to close the deal with Lazio, Hummel has recently entered the fray. The Danish manufacturer is now considered a serious candidate. The company’s current partners include Bournemouth, Real Betis, Coventry City, Werder Bremen, and the Danish national team. (Photo by Marco Rosi – SS Lazio/Getty Images) Supplying Lazio’s Danish duo Oliver Provstgaard and Gustav Isaksen could be an additional incentive for Hummel to collaborate with the Italian capital side. The next few weeks could be decisive on this front.

item.title: 2026-2027 NCAA Women’s Hockey GRaNT Computer Rankings
item.description: ***Have I fallen behind on refreshing the rankings? Don’t hesitate to email me at grant dot salzano at gmail if you’d like the rankings updated!*** GRaNT Computer Rankings: NCAA “National Collegiate” Women’s Hockey Welcome back to the 2026-2027 edition of the GRaNT Computer Rankings! It stands for G rant’s R easonable a nd N ot T errible Computer Rankings. We hope that you find the rating system itself as good as the name. For anyone who has ever complained about NPI, RPI, or the Pairwise, this is another system to stand alongside some of the deeper mathematical methods like KRACH or CHODR that give a more robust and methodologically sound ranking of teams. The following involves math. Skip past this section if that makes you uncomfortable. ========== The ranking system can be most simply described as KRACH for goal differential. Instead of straight goal differential, though, what’s used is a sort of goal ratio, or, more accurately, the percentage of goals scored in a game (we’ll call it “G%”) by each team — for example, if Team A beats Team B by a score of 3-1, then Team A’s G% = 3 out of 4 goals, or 75%, and Team B’s G% = 1 out of 4 goals, or 25%. Each team’s GRaNT rating is used to determine its expected G% against a given team. If Team A has a GRaNT rating of 300 and Team B has a GRaNT rating of 125, over the long run we would expect Team A to score 300/(300+125) ≈ 70.5% of the goals in games against Team B on average — something like a 2.8-1.2 or 3.5-1.5 final score. The GRaNT rankings are determined by setting each team’s rating so that the sum of their expected G%’s against each of their opponents (calculated using each team’s rating as described in the previous paragraph) is equal to the sum of their actual G%’s against each of their opponents (the real-life results of the games that actually happened). A rating of 100 represents an “average” team. Someone with an eagle eye might note that shutouts appear to cause a problem in this method of calculation. A team that wins 1-0 and a team that wins 5-0 will both have a G% of 1.000 for that game, even though a 5-0 win is clearly better. This is handled by doing the math on all of the games as a whole instead of individually. For example, if Team A wins its two games 1-0 and 3-1, its combined G% will be 4 out of 5 goals = 80%, and if Team B wins its two games 5-0 and 3-1, its combined G% will be 8 out of 9 goals = 89%. An added feature of this “G%” figure is that you have diminishing returns on blowouts. So, while winning a game 4-1 (80%) is a reasonable amount better than winning 3-1 (75%), winning a game 8-1 (89%) doesn’t really do that much for you compared to winning 7-1 (88%). Lastly, each team is given a “phantom 1-1 tie” against an “average” team. This has no effect on the relative position of teams in the rankings, but allows the formula to be calculated properly (and prevents any issues for a team that might have played in only shutouts). KRACH’s formula does something similar. ======

Coach Brian Schottenheimer’s Dallas Cowboys found themselves 2-4 heading into Monday Night Football’s clash in Philadelphia amid the dropping of a Dak Prescott truth bomb . Philadelphia is banged up heading into the game judging by the Eagles’ Week 7 injury report , while the Cowboys have injury concerns of their own to worry about. Word broke prior to the game that the Cowboys will be without two players against the Eagles, who will not be traveling with the team to the City of Brotherly Love. “OLB Marist Liufau and S PJ Locke, who were both listed as questionable on Saturday’s game status report, will not be traveling with the team to Philadelphia,” the Cowboys PR account said. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “They will both remain on Reserve/Injured-Designated for Return.” Locke has three tackles this season in two games for the Cowboys. Lifau is a 2024 third-round pick who has not played a game with the Cowboys this season. The Cowboys have been reeling on both sides of the ball with rumors swirling about a potential trade for Cardinals pass rusher Josh Sweat . Philadelphia is also 2-4 headed into the game and has a worse point differential than the Cowboys and even more difficult injury problems to contend with affecting star players DeVonta Smith, Jalen Hurts, Saquon Barkley and others. Monday night’s game feels like a must-win for Schottenheimer and his team if they are to establish any momentum headed toward the NFL season’s midway point. Fans are growing restless after what feels like an endless string of prime time defeats, putting the onus on Prescott and the Cowboys to bring home a huge division win. item.description: Minnesota Vikings safety Harrison Smith recorded his 40th interception to end the game Sunday against the Indianapolis Colts. Getty Minnesota Vikings veteran safety Harrison Smith called game against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday. His pick of quarterback Daniel Jones with a little more than a minute remaining in the fourth quarter ended any hopes of an Indianapolis comeback. It also put Smith in a very exclusive club. The interception was the safety’s 40th of his 15-year NFL career. With the pick, he joined the 40/20 club — 40 interceptions and 20 sacks in a career. There had been hope Ratcliffe, a boyhood United fan, would change that when he struck a deal with the Glazers to become a minority shareholder on Christmas Eve 2023. Instead, a succession of decisions have led to major questions over his handling of the club. On the management side, United's hierarchy eventually backed Erik ten Hag after talking with alternatives in the wake of the shock 2024 FA Cup final triumph over Manchester City, spending over £200m on the likes of Leny Yoro, Matthijs de Ligt and Manuel Ugarte. Last week, Ten Hag told the Athletic the club went back on a promise not to sell homegrown Scotland international Scott McTominay to fund Ugarte's £50m move from Paris St-Germain. item.title: Oregon men's basketball cruises past Stanford in exhibition
item.description: Oregon men’s basketball ended its stretch of preseason exhibition games with a victory against Stanford. Fred Payne had 15 points to lead the Ducks to an 85-57 win Oct. 25 at Matthew Knight Arena. Oregon was buoyed by the presence of 6-foot-10 forward Malique Ewin, a fifth-year transfer from Arkansas who just recently became eligible to play for the Ducks. Ewin had 11 points and five rebounds in 11 minutes of playing time. Sean Stewart had 10 points for Oregon and Taylor Bowen had team highs of six rebounds and four assists. The Ducks led 40-24 at halftime, outshot the Cardinal 50%-31%, won the rebounding battle 39-28 and committed just nine turnovers. Up next for Oregon men's basketball The regular season begins Nov. 2 with a 7 p.m. game against Montana at Matthew Knight Arena. The game will be televised on the Big Ten Network. item.title: Legendary USC receiver unloads on ‘f—ing joke’ Trojans after Lincoln Riley’s latest disaster
item.description: The pressure is mounting on USC head coach Lincoln Riley , and the results aren’t meeting expectations. After the Trojans suffered a devastating loss on the road to the Wisconsin Badgers on Saturday night , Keyshawn Johnson released a 2 two-minute, 42-second video of him calling USC a “F—ing joke.” We really just lost to Wisconsin… Lincoln Riley I respect you but it just ain’t working out. Tough decisions have to be made USC. #USC #FightOn pic.twitter.com/VlYOGlzvEZ — Keyshawn Johnson (@keyshawn) October 25, 2026 Keyshawn Johnson calls USC a “F—ing joke” and to part ways with Lincoln Riley. Getty Images “Enough is enough,” Johnson said after calling out Riley and the Trojans. Johnson opened up the video and said all he could do is “sit here and laugh.” “We really just lost to Wisconsin. Not only did we lose, we got run out of the building,” Johnson said. Johnson went on to call out the poor performance of the Trojans offense on Saturday after they scored one touchdown in the second quarter of a 24-7 loss to Wisconsin. USC quarterback Jayden Maiava looking on ahead of matchup against Wisconsin on Saturday night. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Trojans offense finished the game throwing for 258 yards from quarterback Jayden Maiava, who completed 31 of 50 passes with two interceptions , while the USC offensive line gave up five sacks. USC’s running game had its worst performance of the year, as they combined for -17 rushing yards, while running back King Miller ran the ball 11 times for eight yards. Johnson said he was sick of what he was watching with USC and started to talk about how well UCLA — who just improved to 7-0 with wins against Oregon, Wisconsin, and Michigan State — under first-year head coach Bob Chesney. He also congratulated Wisconsin’s head coach. “Congratulations, Luke Fickell. Coach Fickell, you did an amazing job. You really did. You and your staff put it together,” Johnson said. “Hopefully you get one of these real Power-5 jobs. …Right now, maybe you could be our head coach.” Lincoln Riley looking on in Saturday’s game against the Wisconsin Badgers. AP Photo/Ross Harried Johnson went on to say that he respects Riley and likes him, but thinks a divorce between him and the program is needed. “We gotta recognize and understand that, and make some tough decisions,” Johnson said. “Sometimes tough decisions have got to be made. Whether you want to whether you don’t. They gotta be made.” At the end of the video, Johnson went on to call for the USC financial boosters, administration, and “financial people” to make the tough decision on Riley. If USC chooses to move on from Riley, they would be expected to buy him out at $70 million.

item.title: Max Eberl lauds Bayern Munich’s ‘extraordinary’ effort in overcoming recent hurdles
item.description: MUNICH, GERMANY - OCTOBER 17: Max Eberl, Sporting Director of FC Bayern Muenchen, at the press conference following the team's victory during the Bundesliga 2026/27 match between FC Bayern München and RB Leipzig at Allianz Arena on October 17, 2026 in Munich, Germany. (Photo by F. Noever/FC Bayern via Getty Images) | FC Bayern via Getty Images One does not want to keep mentioning Vincent Kompany’s collapse and Joshua Kimmich’s familial tragedy, aside from sending prayers to the duo and their families and hoping things improve as soon as possible. The truth is that these horrible incidents also affect those around them, including Bayern Munich’s staff and players. Yet, in the midst of a brutal footballing schedule, they have had to carry on as close to normal as possible. Overcoming SC Freiburg away from home is always a difficult task; doing so with 8 absences is even harder, and doing so after dealing with the trauma of recent tragedies is extraordinary. Bayern’s board member for sport, Max Eberl, certainly thinks so. “I don’t think we really understand what we’ve achieved this week with all the hurdles we’ve had to overcome.” Eberl said (as captured by Bayern’s official website ). “What the team and we as a group have done with the coaching staff is extraordinary. The win means three points, but it was a bigger win than just three points. Obviously we’ve got problems at the moment, but we have our squad and are really happy. The team played an almost perfect away game for over 80 minutes. The way we fought to avoid an equalizer at the end and then made it 3-1. It was a really great win today.” Join the conversation! item.title: Vikings just proved why nobody wants to face Minnesota
item.description: Vikings just proved why nobody wants to face Minnesota originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Another week, another win for the reigning NFC North darlings, the Minnesota Vikings . The team pulled off a comfortable 16-10 victory over the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday, putting themselves in a solid position near the top of the NFC North once again. It's been an exciting run through the NFL's Week 7 slate, and the Vikings were one of the teams worth watching. They're showing off an impressive defense, which isn't something you see all the time in the NFL. The league is largely offense-driven, after all, so watching a genuinely dominant defense is a treat. The Minnesota Vikings' dominant defense is carrying the team, but their offense still has some work to do Dan Parr of the NFL's official website offers some takeaways from the NFL's run of Week 7 games . He praises the Vikings' defense while raising questions about their offense. "Minnesota is allowing a league-low 12.3 points per game and has won 11 straight games dating back to Week 14 of the 2025 season, the longest active winning streak in the NFL," he notes. So, the reason the Vikings are so difficult to face isn't necessarily their offense. It's their defense. "The Colts were leading, 10-6, at halftime, but they were shut out in the second half, and Jones finished 13 of 22 for just 108 yards," he adds. He also points out that two missed field goals thanks to Spencer Shrader "helped the Vikings' cause, but so did a suffocating defense that generated a 55.6% pressure rate and four sacks." The Vikings' defense held Indianapolis scoreless in the second half, and they really pressured the quarterback, Daniel Jones, throughout the game. Then, the Vikings sealed the win with Harrison Smith's interception. As Ice Cube says, it was a good day. item.title: Knicks' Mike Brown outlines initial plans for former Lakers guard
item.description: Knicks' Mike Brown outlines initial plans for former Lakers guard originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . While the offseason is firmly in the rearview mirror, teams around the association are still making moves to improve their rosters, with the New York Knicks being no different. Earlier in the week, the Knicks signed Dalton Knecht to a two-way deal, bringing the former first-round pick's brief time in the free-agent pool to an end. Knecht was waived by the Los Angeles Lakers earlier in the month after a two-year stint in the City of Angels that saw him somewhat struggle to adapt to life in the NBA. Across 132 games with the Lakers, Knecht averaged 7.1 points per game, but the real blow to his stock would come in his second season in Los Angeles, which saw his scoring average dip by five points. Given that the Knicks' roster seems to be fairly stacked, there were some questions about how the team will utilize Knecht, and on Sunday night, head coach Mike Brown filled in the NBA world. Knecht will feature for the Knicks' G League roster for the time being Mike Brown says Knicks want Dalton Knecht to play as much as possible to the plan initially is to have in Westchester playing games with the Knicks' G League team. — Ian Begley (@IanBegley) October 25, 2026 As reported by SNYTV's Ian Begley, New York wants the former first-round pick to get as many reps in as possible, which will lead to him being used at the G League level with the West Chester Knicks. This shouldn't come as too much of a shock given that Knecht signed a two-way contract, which allows the player to be used at both the NBA and G League level. For what it's worth, this isn't exactly a bad thing either, as the Knicks have made use of their two-way stars in years past, including Landry Shamet, who featured in 27 games during the 2024-25 season for West Chester. The West Chester Knicks are slated to get their season underway on November 6th, with a match against the Maine Celtics, the G League affiliate of the Boston Celtics , so that could be the first look fans have at Dalton Knecht at the G League level since his move. item.title: Chiefs-Seahawks Inactives: TE Jared Wiley active for first time in 2026
item.description: KANSAS CITY, MO - DECEMBER 25: Jared Wiley #12 of the Kansas City Chiefs looks on from the field during an NFL football game against the Denver Broncos at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium on December 25, 2025 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs have released their list of inactive players for Sunday’s game against the Seattle Seahawks . Tackle Jaylon Moore, wide receiver Rashee Rice, cornerback Jadon Canady, fullback Ben VanSumeren and defensive end Jack Pyburn will not dress. Rookie Garrett Nussmeir has been designated as the third quarterback and is eligible to enter the game should starter Patrick Mahomes and backup Justin Fields become unavailable. Our inactives for tonight's SNF matchup against the Seahawks ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/iViYLpYBzc — Kansas City Chiefs (@Chiefs) October 25, 2026 Moore (concussion) and Rice (hamstring) had already been ruled out on Friday’s final injury report . Not listed are tackle Josh Simmons (back) and running back Brashard Smith (hamstring) who were placed the team’s Reserve/Injured list this week and will be sidelined for at least the next four weeks. With Moore and Simmons unavailable, rookie tackle Diego Pounds will suit up for his first NFL contest. Kansas City acquired Pounds — who played the last two seasons at Ole Miss — via trade from the Baltimore Ravens on August 30. Pounds signed with Baltimore as an undrafted free agent this spring. Veteran Joshua Ezeudu is expected to start at right tackle in place of Moore. Cornerback L’Jarius Sneed (knee) was listed as questionable on Friday. We also learned on Saturday that, due to a personal reason, Sneed would not travel to Seattle with the team but planned to meet them for the game. Sneed is active for the contest. Tight end Jared Wiley is active for the first time this season. Wiley had been a healthy scratch in Kansas City’s first five games. The Chiefs have all four rostered tight ends available for Sunday night. On Saturday, Kansas City elevated practice squad wide receiver Justin Watson to the active roster. As an elevated player, he will automatically be returned to the team’s practice squad after the game. It will be Watson’s second of three permitted elevations. The Seahawks have also released their list of inactives. Tonight’s @Seahawks inactives; QB Drew Lock will serve as the emergency 3rd quarterback. pic.twitter.com/OzEKzer0eH — Seahawks PR (@seahawksPR) October 25, 2026 Notably, running back Zach Charbonnet (knee) — who split time with now Chiefs star Kenneth Walker in recent seasons — will not suit up. Charbonnet had already been ruled out on Friday as he continues working his way back from an ACL injury suffered in the postseason. The Seahawks had already ruled out linebackers Chazz Surratt (calf) and Beau Stephens (ankle). Linebacker Connor O’Toole (hamstring) is also inactive despite ending the week with a questionable tag. Running back Robert Henry appears to be a healthy scratch.

item.title: Jose Mourinho: “The group is strong and very united, even in the most difficult moments”
item.description: BARCELONA, SPAIN - OCTOBER 25: Head coach Jose Mourinho of Real Madrid walks onto the pitch at the end of the LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 match between FC Barcelona and Real Madrid at Spotify Camp Nou on October 25, 2026 in Barcelona, Spain. (Photo by Pedro Salado/Getty Images) | Getty Images Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho spoke to the media after their win over Barcelona on Sunday. Talking about whether this win could be Real Madrid’s turning point, he said: “This match is one where we went into it three, six, or nine points behind. Obviously, going in nine points is psychologically tough. Going in six points is balanced, even with a direct clash at the Bernabéu. Going in three points is different. Obviously. And the way we won is also different. Because you can win with luck, but we did it calmly and deservedly. Regarding the choice of Bernardo… I’ve only been here for a little over three months. And although I know him well, that’s one thing, and knowing how he can integrate into the team dynamic is another. The group is very strong. I’ll never say that this is my starting eleven or that this is undisputed, because the squad is very good, complete. The players work very hard. Everyone is prepared. And that’s life. You’ve already asked me two questions, and neither about Lunin, but if we lose here because of his mistakes, the first or second question would be about him. I’ve only told him, ‘You train to play, not to sit on the bench, go and play.’ And he played a very balanced and calm game. We have the The best goalkeeper in the world, but today none of us cried because Thibaut wasn’t playing. The group is strong and very united, even in the most difficult moments. Five wins in a row, and that’s it. Another game on Sunday, with a nice run, because we play away, then away on Wednesday, and then, another gift, away again… on Saturday. But… come on. There’s another name I couldn’t leave out: Valverde played injured for more than 40 minutes. Because he got injured, he wanted to keep going, to continue, to push himself to his limits. And he gave everything while he was on the field.” Mourinho on the game “First of all, I think it was a great match. A high-level game. One that the whole football-loving world surely stopped to watch. And they weren’t disappointed, with two teams that played to win. In our case, I’m more concerned with talking about my own team: the lads played an extraordinary match. But a great match, a great victory. The lads deserve it.” Mourinho on Eduardo Camavinga “Camavinga, like everyone else, is a starter. They all train to play. Then it’s the coach who has to decide. Sometimes they want to make changes, they look to the bench, and there are many coaches who suffer because they don’t have solutions, because they aren’t able to implement their ideas. And I have a deep bench. Camavinga played an extraordinary match against Leipzig; today he was on the bench. Flick brought on De Jong, who has incredible stamina, and against a Bernardo who had been training with Pedri for a long time… Well, the game needed fresh legs to keep marking, to launch counter-attacks. And I told Cama that, obviously, it was Tchouameni who was marking him because of his characteristics and yellow card… and he had to attack spaces, something that’s difficult against Barcelona, ​​because many times you attack and you’re offside or the goalkeeper is out of position. If the movement comes from midfield, as Camavinga did, it’s more difficult for them. Things went well. Great game; the team deserved more.” Mourinho on the game’s difficulty “It was the most difficult match, against the highest quality opponent, one that had only won in the league. For us, it’s the victory with the most impressive performance.” Mourinho on improvements since Atletico “The truth is, we’ve improved a lot in the last few matches, there’s no denying that. But the two wins we’ve had… I don’t want to dwell on the Atlético game, but the Betis game was the away match where we created the most chances. We missed a lot, Espí’s goal was disallowed by a millimeter. It’s not like we were a disaster. The group is doing well, with tremendous camaraderie among everyone. The fans on the sidelines support those on the inside. It’s a great group to work with. And these are the kinds of groups that come together in difficult times. When we lost to Atlético, the next day everyone forgot how we lost. Stay calm, keep going. That’s it. On to the next one. This is a great victory, but when we get back to work… I’m not going to let people get carried away. If we win today and lose at El Sardinero, it’ll be the same story, because Real Madrid doesn’t play to win at the Camp Nou, but to win the league. We have to keep going.” Mourinho on Marc Cucurella “We have two top-level left-backs, which allows me to manage their playing time a bit. Carreras played on Wednesday, and that allowed Cucu to be fresh, focused, and thinking only about this match. Obviously, he played against a great player, but he’s his teammate, and he knows him well. I always say that I only understand how good players are when I see them in front of me, when I’m on the touchline. Watching them on TV, I miss something. It’s when they’re ten meters away that I understand the quality of the players. The kid is very good, but he’s also clever. He tried everything to get Cucu a yellow card, but he held his own well, and Diomande very rarely gave Espart or Cancelo an advantage. A great team effort. But Cucu… he was very good against a very good kid.” Mourinho on the credit for this win “No, no. It’s for the players. It’s our life, the coach’s life. That’s why, week after week, coaches lose their jobs. But that’s the way it is. And in this case, I’m incredibly happy that it’s like this. The players deserve it. They deserve it. It’s much harder to be on the field and play than on the bench and make decisions. I’m very, very happy for them. For all of them. For Asencio, who had surgery a week ago and wanted to come today, to be here, next to his teammates on the bench.” Mourinho on tactical changes since Roma “I have an extraordinary group, with all the players possessing the quality and mentality to play. I think the forwards also like this mix, because it gives us balance in defense and more quality when building from the back in the defensive organisation.”

The lack of conversion consistency repeatedly stalled drives, none more glaring than a 3-and-out midway through the fourth quarter where three consecutive plays generated just eight yards . item.title: Mbappé double secures Real Madrid late victory at Barcelona after Raphinha leveller
item.description: Thirteen years later, José Mourinho led Real Madrid into the Camp Nou as one team and them out again as another having secured the kind of late victory he loves and which opens up a whole new world. With just three minutes and the final reserves of energy remaining, a wonderful moment of skill from Jude Bellingham found Eduardo Camavinga and set them on one last run. Camavinga sprinted free, skilfully slipped Pau Cubarsí and pulled back for Kylian Mbappé to provide the finish, a little bit of history written. “The world that loves football will have stopped to this and they won’t have gone disappointed; this was two teams that played to win,” Mourinho said. It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and it was his team that won it. Arriving right on time, Mbappé scored his second to make it 2-1, the Camp Nou falling quiet and their team given no time to react. They had drawn level after Mbappé’s opener, Raphinha scoring, but could not do it again. Continue reading...

item.title: Ballon d’Or ceremony returns to England in nod to ‘revolutionary’ Stanley Matthews
item.description: Matthews’ family ‘very excited’ as London Palladium hosts event 70 years after first award at Blackpool town hall When football’s dignitaries assemble on Monday at the London Palladium for the Ballon d’Or ceremony it will be a far cry from the first awards 70 years ago. That was held in the slightly less glamorous surroundings of Blackpool town hall, where Stanley Matthews was presented with the prize by Gabriel Hanot, the visionary editor of L’Équipe who came up with the idea of crowning the world’s best player every year. A specially commissioned china plate was also handed over by the town’s mayor before the 41-year-old Matthews, who was famously teetotal, gave a short speech. “He might have had a double carrot juice that day,” says his son, Stanley Matthews Jr, who will attend this year’s awards with his sister, Jean, and her two daughters. “There was no ceremony. ‘Here’s your Ballon d’Or, well done’, sort of thing. But obviously it’s grown over the years, and now it’s a huge event. We’re very excited.” Continue reading...

item.title: Tottenham stun Chelsea for second league win in a week as Cole Palmer is sent off
item.description: There are days when Tottenham go into these big games and find ways to beat themselves. This time, though, they held their nerve at a ground where they have mostly only known doom. Spurs played with control, stayed patient and won at Stamford Bridge for the first time since 2018 after waiting for Chelsea to press the self-destruct button during a calamitous and comical ending to a cagey game. Chelsea were meant to have grown. Xabi Alonso had even praised his side’s emotional control and ability to manage awkward spells during the buildup, but perhaps that was asking for trouble. Chelsea, short of poise on and off the pitch, deserved to be beaten at home for the first time this season and there was plenty of blame to go around after Alonso got his tactics wrong, Mike Penders scored a ridiculous own goal and Cole Palmer was sent off after a lunge on Conor Gallagher when he was already on a booking. Nicolas Jackson’s double earned Aston Villa a 2-1 victory at Villa Park after Guéhi was unable to control the ball for the opener. Instead he spilled it into the path of John McGinn, who played it to Jackson, allowing him to score the first of two goals. item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: WSL talking points: pressure mounts on Slegers as Hemp closes on record
item.description: Another round of games and another disappointing draw for Arsenal while Manchester City sit top of the table with a 100% record There would have been hope that the international break could offer the Arsenal players and staff a reset but the same problems reared their head at the Emirates on Sunday in a 1-1 draw with Birmingham. As they have done so often this season, the Gunners dominated most attacking and possession-based metrics – they registered 76% possession, a 2.73 xG and 43 touches in the opposition box – but their profligacy in front of goal and lack of urgency in their play once again came to the fore. Of their 27 chances, they managed just four on target as they toiled against a resilient opposition who understood the playbook. Birmingham set up in a strong defensive structure, protecting their box admirably with numbers to frustrate Renée Slegers’s side, who famously struggle to break down low blocks. In contrast, Birmingham scored with their one shot on target as Océane Hurtré took her impressive tally to six in six. Sophie Downey Match report: Arsenal 1-1 Birmingham Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
